Iron deficiency is a fairly prevalent problem in pre-menopausal women. According to the NHANES 
III data (1994–1998), 5 percent of women aged 20 to 49 have iron deficiency anemia, and 11 percent 
have iron deficiency without anemia. The prevalence of iron deficiency was similar in NHANES 
III and NHANES 1999–2000 in most age and sex groups, but newer data from NHANES 2003–
2006 found that the prevalence of iron deficiency without anemia had increased to 12 percent 
among females age 20 to 49.
